title: The 4 Disciplines of Execution
author: Chris McChesney, Sean Covey, and Jim Huling
blurb: Most leaders can set a strategy. Far fewer can get it done. This book argues that the real enemy of execution is not laziness or bad ideas but the whirlwind, the endless urgent work that keeps the day running and swallows everything new. To break through, the authors offer four disciplines. First, focus on one or two wildly important goals instead of many. Second, act on lead measures, the small actions you control that drive results, rather than obsessing over lagging outcomes. Third, keep a simple, compelling scoreboard so the team always knows whether it is winning. Fourth, create a cadence of accountability through short weekly meetings where everyone commits to specific actions. Together, these disciplines turn vague strategy into steady, visible progress, even while the whirlwind keeps blowing.

lessons.b: The biggest threat to any important goal is the whirlwind, the urgent daily work that consumes the time and energy needed for anything new.
